- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., >3 consecutive negative values), reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to account for bearish momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% above recent mean), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If model forecasts a steep downward trend (e.g., >3 consecutive drops >2% from prior day), check for mean reversion — if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, adjust upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bearish bias.  
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive but model shows strong downward bias, add 1–3% to forecast to reflect potential rebound.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently overpredicts by >2% in early days (e.g., first 7–10 days), reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to align with observed lag.  
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >2 consecutive positive values), model often overestimates — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overreaction.
